content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Timothy Wallace (E022), requesting admin access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes that conflict:
- Note 1: full-time Engineer, recommends write for Payroll
- Note 2: contractor with basic security training, recommends read for Payroll; says earlier note outdated/incorrect

The Security DB note (Note 2) says the employee is a contractor with basic security training. This seems to be more authoritative/specific - it explicitly says the earlier memory note was outdated/incorrect.

Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system. Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist, not Engineer. So max is write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training, max is read.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested is admin, which is above max, so grant max = read.

The requested level is admin. The maximum is read (per the contractor note). Grant read.

So the decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB shows contractor with basic security training; contractors max at read; admin never allowed for contractors. Requested admin is above max, so grant read.
